A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Traffic-R1 work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original traffic simulations, incident-handling evaluations, capability comparisons, ablations and a six-week deployment study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports deployment inference latency and average output length.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-3B model, offline expert-guided GRPO, online STPO and alternating two-group communication procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 provides implementation detail for the existing communication design rather than establishing a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same expert dataset, simulated training network, Jinan and Hangzhou datasets, 200 incident examples, emergency-vehicle scenario, general-capability benchmarks and ten-intersection deployment. Newly cited benchmarks are not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 3 and 5, including CoLLMLight in Table 2 and LALight in Table 3. The deployment comparator changes its label from Original Pipeline to Manual, but remains the same human-operated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported simulation durations, phase timings, metrics, baseline training arrangements and 5% emergency-vehicle flow remain unchanged. Both deployment studies alternate systems weekly over six weeks and exclude weekends and holidays. Newly specified hardware documents implementation rather than a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: Figures 5 and 6 retain identical capability comparisons and expert-stage, open-world-stage and communication ablations. Appendix A.5 retains the same five reasoning cases. The new limitations discussion adds no robustness or failure-analysis experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error-bar reporting. Dataset summary statistics and the point-estimate reporting in the empirical figures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Benchmark tables, capability and ablation plots, and field-study values are unchanged. Appendix A.6.1 newly reports average inference latency below two seconds with 437 output tokens on average. Table 6 repeats existing deployment results rather than adding another experiment.

T1.justification: v2 omits v1 Section 3's explicit problem statement and Equation 1 mapping observations, incidents and messages to reasoning and actions. The road-network, phase and control-system definitions and the GRPO/STPO mathematics remain equivalent; no proofs or guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a compact two-stage RL controller, zero-shot generalization, explainable reasoning, asynchronous coordination and practical deployment. Rewriting the abstract, introduction and conclusion does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 8 identifies information loss from structured textual inputs and missing large-scale hallucination and driver-feedback evaluations. Appendix A.6 distinguishes current centralized deployment from future edge execution. Conversely, Section 5.3 broadens the over-30% OOD superiority wording to larger general LLMs, which unchanged Table 3 does not support.

D1.justification: v2 specifies four H100 training GPUs, the Verl framework and Tesla T40 inference hardware. It expands the input template and adds communication pseudocode documenting message buffers and a 2 km distance condition. These are new disclosures; the dataset-generation prose becomes less specific by replacing the explicit DeepSeek-R1 proposer name with a generic base model.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including TrafficGPT, DiLu, CityBench, UrbanVideo-bench and HybridFlow, while removing the SUMO reference. These broaden supporting literature without substantially changing the positioning against traditional RL, LLM explainers and LLM assistants.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and substantial method and results passages are rewritten and condensed. Deployment details move from Section 6 into Appendix A.6, appendix subsections are reordered, and a separate Limitations section is introduced.

P2.justification: The document undergoes comprehensive changes to page geometry, typography, captions and figure/table sizing and placement. Deployment figures are relocated and renumbered, field results are duplicated in Table 6, and Algorithm 1 is added. Most underlying graphics and numerical table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Hardware disclosures, expanded communication documentation and explicit validation limitations make the unchanged research easier to assess and reproduce. These are limited transparency gains. A countervailing weakness is the broader OOD superiority wording: Table 3 still reports Traffic-R1 EAA of 0.85 versus 0.88 for Qwen2.5 and 0.93 for DeepSeek-R1.
